level: stop-fence slice 5 hardening, component level: bounded retry for transient atomic-JSON rename failures on Windows; no product entry point and no activation
componentAcceptance: Win11 / Node v24.20.0, offline: the seven related suites total 64 tests, 63 pass, 0 fail, 1 explicit skip (the Linux-only writer-advisory case 22). Four deterministic helper cases cover EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY, success at the retry bound, exhaustion and immediate non-transient failure. Eight no-wrapper configuration-commit repetitions contain zero rename failures; seven runs are 12/12 and one retains the separate pre-existing MIGRATION_COMMIT_SOURCE_CHANGED flake. Final root regression: 1893 tests, 1824 pass, 0 fail, 69 skipped.
productAcceptance: None. This change only retries the atomic publication of fence records and migration-gate.json. It does not prove old-process stop-write behavior, wire the orchestration into a product entry, add an activate->committed path, or change activationSupported / postActivationRollbackSupported / stopWriteProvable. Package and acceptance scores remain 0/20, 1/63 and M0 11/12.
implementation: A shared internal renameMigrationFile helper performs the first rename plus at most five retries at fixed 50ms intervals, only for EPERM, EACCES and EBUSY. Other errors are thrown immediately and exhaustion rethrows the last original error.

Both fence atomicJson and configuration-commit atomicJson use the helper. Temp-file creation, write, fsync, close, finally cleanup and non-Windows directory sync are unchanged; retries never accept partial JSON or relax strict reads.

The temporary test-side EPERM wrappers in both orchestration suites and the native crash-loop retry were removed. Crash injection again requires the original child to exit 86 on its first run, so product behavior rather than an operator retry is tested.
Four deterministic tests are registered in npm test. They verify all three transient codes, success on attempt six, six-attempt exhaustion with five delays, and no retry or sleep for ENOENT.

limitations: Retry coverage is deliberately limited to atomic JSON publication in migration-fence.mjs and migration-configuration-commit.mjs. The distinct configuration-file retirement rename and other repository rename sites are unchanged.
Retry handles transient sharing/AV-style errors only; persistent permission, read-only filesystem, missing-path and corruption failures remain fail-closed.
